caption:
Koko joined a walking group and picked up the pace. Now the front of her shins aches whenever she walks faster.

The muscle at the front of the shin lifts your foot as you swing your leg, then lowers it gently each time you land. Longer strides and a sudden jump in speed can give it a lot more work to do.

Hybi's 1-minute routine: seated toe raises, lower over 3 seconds, 15 reps twice a day. Build your pace gradually and try slightly shorter steps.

One sore spot on the bone, or aching at rest, is worth an assessment. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio 🐨
